data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's own countercondition explicitly concedes that anthropogenic heat flux or impervious cover could be the better predictor of cross-city UHI variation. If the target already identifies a condition under which its central claim fails, and that condition corresponds to a widely documented empirical reality — impervious surface fraction is one of the most robust cross-city predictors of UHI magnitude — then the claim that sky view factor is the 'single best' mechanism is self-undermining rather than conclusively argued. The target presents no evidence or argument excluding impervious cover and anthropogenic heat as superior predictors; it merely stipulates sky view primacy while flagging the alternative as live.
